questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: The two inseparable meanings of the conjugal act in personalist ethics are:
questions.rationale: The conjugal act has integrated unitive (love-giving) and procreative (life-giving) dimensions.
questions.source: Udan, Healthcare Ethics (2023), Ch. 3.1 Sexual ethics (PDF p. 81)
questions.quote: The conjugal act has inseparable and integrated unitive, and procreative dimensions.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: The Family Code of the Philippines defines marriage as a special contract of permanent union between:
questions.rationale: Article 1 of the Family Code (EO 209, 1987) defines marriage as a permanent union between a man and a woman.
questions.source: Udan, Healthcare Ethics (2023), Ch. 3.1 Fundamentals of marriage (PDF p. 83)
questions.quote: a special contract of pennanent union between a man and a woman entered into in accordance with law

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: Under Article 45 of the Family Code, a marriage of a 19-year-old without parental consent is:
questions.rationale: Marriage of a party 18 to below 21 without parental consent is a ground for annulment, unless they freely cohabited afterward.
questions.source: Udan, Healthcare Ethics (2023), Ch. 3.1 Family Code, Art. 45 (PDF p. 84)
questions.quote: Marriage for those 18 years of age or over but below 21 and the marriage was solemnized without the consent of the parents

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: Under Article 45, consent to marriage obtained by force or intimidation makes the marriage:
questions.rationale: Consent obtained by force, intimidation or undue influence is a ground for annulment.
questions.source: Udan, Healthcare Ethics (2023), Ch. 3.1 Family Code, Art. 45 (PDF p. 84)
questions.quote: Consent was obtained by force, intimidation or undue influence.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: A wife files for legal separation because her husband has repeatedly beaten her. This ground is under:
questions.rationale: Repeated physical violence or grossly abusive conduct is a ground for legal separation under Article 55.
questions.source: Udan, Healthcare Ethics (2023), Ch. 3.1 Family Code, Art. 55 (PDF p. 84)
questions.quote: Repeated physical violence or grossly abusive conduct

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: In Humanae Vitae, marital love that goes beyond the couple to raise new life is described as:
questions.rationale: Marital love is human, total, faithful, exclusive and fruitful; fruitful love is destined to raise new life.
questions.source: Udan, Healthcare Ethics (2023), Ch. 3.1 Characteristics of marital love (PDF p. 83)
questions.quote: Fruitful - love goes beyond couple, destined to raise up new life

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: In gestational surrogacy, the surrogate carries an embryo made from:
questions.rationale: Gestational surrogacy transfers IVF embryos from the intended mother's or a donor's eggs; traditional surrogacy uses the surrogate's egg.
questions.source: Udan, Healthcare Ethics (2023), Ch. 3.1 Surrogate motherhood (PDF p. 87)
questions.quote: Gestational surrogacy is performed by transferring embryos made through IVF with eggs from the intended mother or a donor.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: Fertilization of an egg in a laboratory dish, with the embryo then placed in the uterus, is:
questions.rationale: IVF ('in glass') achieves conception outside the woman's body, then transfers the embryo for gestation.
questions.source: Udan, Healthcare Ethics (2023), Ch. 3.1 In-vitro fertilization (PDF p. 87)
questions.quote: In vitro (in glass) human fertilization is facilitating conception of a human person outside the body of a woman.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: A couple undergoing IVF asks the nurse for her opinion. The nurse's best role is to:
questions.rationale: The nurse assists non-judgmentally, offers information and supports the patient's informed, free choice.
questions.source: Udan, Healthcare Ethics (2023), Ch. 3.1 Morality of artificial reproduction (PDF p. 88)
questions.quote: to assist the person who is facing issues on artificial reproduction in a non-judgmental manner

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: A woman at 10 weeks has light bleeding and a closed cervix. This is a(n):
questions.rationale: Threatened abortion: bleeding with a closed cervix; the pregnancy may or may not be lost.
questions.source: Udan, Healthcare Ethics (2023), Ch. 3.1 Types of abortion (PDF p. 88)
questions.quote: the cervix is not dilated, and abortion may or may not occur

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: A woman has heavy bleeding and a dilated cervix; loss of the pregnancy is certain. This is a(n):
questions.rationale: Inevitable abortion: profuse bleeding with cervical dilation; abortion will invariably occur.
questions.source: Udan, Healthcare Ethics (2023), Ch. 3.1 Types of abortion (PDF p. 88)
questions.quote: the cervix has become dilated, and abortion will invariably occur

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: After a miscarriage, some placental tissue remains in the uterus. This is a(n):
questions.rationale: Incomplete abortion: some products of conception are retained.
questions.source: Udan, Healthcare Ethics (2023), Ch. 3.1 Types of abortion (PDF p. 88)
questions.quote: Incomplete Abortion • that with retention of parts of the products of conception.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: Which provision of the 1987 Constitution protects the life of the unborn from conception?
questions.rationale: Art. II Sec. 12 recognizes the sanctity of family life and equally protects the life of the mother and the unborn from conception.
questions.source: Udan, Healthcare Ethics (2023), Ch. 3.1 Legal considerations on abortion (PDF p. 88)
questions.quote: It shall equally protect the life of the mother and the life of the unborn from conception.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: Discouraging reproduction among people with presumed 'undesirable' inherited traits is:
questions.rationale: Negative eugenics discourages reproduction by persons with genetic defects; positive eugenics encourages those with 'desirable' traits.
questions.source: Udan, Healthcare Ethics (2023), Ch. 3.1 Eugenics (PDF p. 89)
questions.quote: discouraging reproduction by persons having genetic defects or presumed to have inheritable undesirable traits

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: Below what total fertility rate can a population no longer replace itself?
questions.rationale: A total fertility rate of about 2.1 is the replacement level.
questions.source: Udan, Healthcare Ethics (2023), Ch. 3.1 Demographic winter (PDF p. 92)
questions.quote: fertility has fallen below the accepted 2.1 replacement rate

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: An LGBT patient comes for counseling after self-harm. The nurse's approach should be:
questions.rationale: Guided by respect for persons, nurses give non-judgmental, appropriate care; LGBT groups have higher rates of mental health problems and self-harm.
questions.source: Udan, Healthcare Ethics (2023), Ch. 3.1 On homosexuality (PDF p. 85)
questions.quote: are to carry out without judgment the case-and- age-appropriate interventions
